overview: Truro Cathedral rises over the middle of Cornwall’s only city. It’s younger than it looks: it was built between 1880 and 1910 in Gothic Revival style, after Cornwall won back a diocese of its own, on the site of the old parish church of St Mary.

It’s a peaceful place to step into from the busy streets, and it welcomes visitors of all faiths and none. There’s often something on, from choir concerts and exhibitions to evening light and sound shows.

expect.title: The building
expect.text: A Gothic Revival cathedral right in the heart of the city.

expect.title: Music and events
expect.text: Choral services, concerts, talks, exhibitions and occasional immersive light shows run through the year.

goodToKnow.label: Opening
goodToKnow.text: Visiting hours can change around services and events, so check the opening hours page before you go.

goodToKnow.label: Events
goodToKnow.text: Concerts and shows usually need tickets; see the What’s On page.

week.text: An easy stop to build into a day in Truro, especially on a wet one: combine it with the Cornwall Museum and Art Gallery next door and a wander round the city’s shops.

pairWith.why: Cornwall’s county museum, a few steps away
a small Victorian park in the city
gardens on the Fal estuary just south of the city
